html

html Components
  • Page A page of a stack, as this platform serves one: a document of its own on a static site and a route in route mode, written as the whole window with every other page pruned.
  • Stack A stack of pages, which a document never shows whole: each page is written out as the window with the stack standing for that page alone.
  • Window A window is a surface: html writes its document from the first that no `if` over state and no `for` can take away, which is the page, and shows every other as a `<dialog>` in it, without a backdrop as a desktop window is.
  • draw
  • element The element every tag resolves to.
  • flow The two elements a flow is built from.
  • inline
  • markup.bold
  • markup.codeBlock A class rather than the base's inline style, so the box has a dark half and a page's own `pre` rule can still restyle it.
  • markup.image `<img>` is a void element, so the description has nowhere to go but the attribute it is already a string for.
  • markup.italic
  • markup.link
  • markup.list A list is the element html has for one, so a screen reader announces its length and each item's place, and the browser numbers it and picks a nested list's bullet itself.
  • markup.listItem A task item is a checkbox in place of the bullet: a real one, so it reads as a checkbox, and disabled, since a document describes state rather than holding it.
  • markup.monospace
  • markup.richText `preWrap` is the family's literal-whitespace rule, and html is the one host that would otherwise collapse what the author wrote.
  • markup.run The general run, and the one member with a style to map.
  • markup.strike
  • markup.text
  • markup.token A class, so what a keyword looks like stays the page's to say: the default palette is the class's rule in the stylesheet, light and dark, and a page's own CSS for `sngl-tok-<kind>` wins over it.
  • markup.underline
  • nav.link A link is an address here: the page's href, filled from the params it passes.
  • nav.page
  • nav.stack
  • platform The `html` node of a build directive: `output { none { html() } }`.
  • shapes.canvasImage
  • shapes.canvasText
  • shapes.circle
  • shapes.ellipse
  • shapes.line A line has no interior, so `fill` is not read here at all rather than being set and ignored.
  • shapes.path
  • shapes.rect Each shape sets only the style it uses, which is the point of writing these in SNGL: the translation they replace applied all six properties to every shape, including a font to a rectangle.
  • time.timer `enabled` is the effect's *position*, not part of its key: an effect lives as long as the branch it is written in, so `if enabled` is what makes toggling the gate a mount and an unmount.
  • ui.avatar
  • ui.badge
  • ui.button `@longPress` maps to `contextmenu`, which is what a sustained touch press fires -- and a right-click, which is not the same gesture.
  • ui.card
  • ui.checkbox
  • ui.chip
  • ui.datepicker An empty `value` is what `<input type="date">` shows as unfilled, so an unpicked date is the empty string rather than the zero date.
  • ui.divider
  • ui.drawer
  • ui.hbox
  • ui.image
  • ui.input
  • ui.link
  • ui.menu
  • ui.menubar
  • ui.modal
  • ui.popover
  • ui.progress `<progress>` with no `value` attribute is HTML's own indeterminate bar, so the absent value is spelled by leaving the attribute off rather than by choosing a number to stand for "unknown".
  • ui.radio
  • ui.scroll `@scrollEnd` is the standard library's name for the event the DOM calls `scrollend`.
  • ui.select
  • ui.spacer
  • ui.spinner
  • ui.splitview
  • ui.stack
  • ui.table
  • ui.tabs
  • ui.text
  • ui.textarea
  • ui.toggle
  • ui.toolbar
  • ui.tooltip
  • ui.tree
  • ui.vbox
  • ui.window The window's `@error` is the outermost boundary of what it renders, and catches whether or not the call site handles one.
    • Types
  • DrawContext --- Drawing --- A canvas draws through a CanvasRenderingContext2D, and its methods are the drawing vocabulary.
  • DrawEvent The primitive an override paints through: `@draw` is the target calling in with the context, and the handler body is what the draw function emits.
    • Functions
  • backend Force v to run server-side (back-end).
  • clearInterval
  • cssColor `rgba(...)` as the DOM spells it.
  • drawImage The page's own image shim, which carries the decode cache and the wait for a source that has not arrived yet.
  • frontend Force v to run client-side (front-end).
  • paintStyle Fill and stroke are gated on alpha, which every other backend does and this one did not: the old translation tested the colour *object* for truthiness, and a JS object is always truthy, so a fill-only shape also painted an invisible stroke (#225).
  • roleTag The element a flow's role names.
  • serve Serves dir over HTTP at listen, ":0" when empty, printing the address, until the process is stopped.
  • setInterval --- The timer --- The web already schedules, so this platform needs no timer primitive: the setInterval/clearInterval pair is a lifetime with a thing to release, which is what `effect` brackets.
